missions.name: Program 661A Test A
missions.thruster: EOS cesium contact ion engine (~7 cm)
models: EOS cesium contact ion engine (Program 661A / SNAPSHOT)
missions.target_or_role: Ion propulsion flight test
missions.flight_performance: 0 min beam operation: high-voltage breakdowns, beam supply failed (gas vented from batteries)
missions.notes: Contact-ionization electrostatic thruster, not electron-bombardment. Reached space but engine never thrusted.

missions.name: SERT-1
missions.thruster: NASA LeRC 10 cm mercury electron-bombardment (Kaufman) ion engine; Hughes 8 cm cesium contact ion engine
models: SERT-I cesium contact ion engine (8 cm)
missions.target_or_role: Space Electric Rocket Test: first successful in-space ion engine operation
missions.flight_performance: Mercury engine operated 31 min (28 mN, ~4900 s), 53 HV recycles; cesium engine could not start (HV short)
missions.notes: Cesium contact engine failed to start.

missions.name: Program 661A Test B
missions.thruster: EOS cesium contact ion engine (~7 cm)
models: EOS cesium contact ion engine (Program 661A / SNAPSHOT)
missions.target_or_role: Ion propulsion flight test
missions.flight_performance: ~19 min operation, full beam current 94 mA; spacecraft potential ~-1000 V (inadequate neutralization)
missions.notes: Contact-ionization thruster.

missions.name: Program 661A Test C
missions.thruster: EOS cesium contact ion engine (~7 cm)
models: EOS cesium contact ion engine (Program 661A / SNAPSHOT)
missions.target_or_role: Ion propulsion flight test
missions.flight_performance: ~4 min operation, reached ~20 % of full thrust before re-entry
missions.notes: Contact-ionization thruster.

missions.name: SNAPSHOT (SNAP-10A)
models: EOS cesium contact ion engine (Program 661A / SNAPSHOT)
missions.target_or_role: Secondary payload on the SNAP-10A nuclear reactor test
missions.status: Engine commanded off permanently after <1 h
missions.flight_performance: <1 h operation (~8.5 mN); HV arcing caused EMI and false horizon-sensor signals
missions.notes: Contact-ionization thruster; first ion engine in orbit (reactor-powered spacecraft, engine ran on batteries).

missions.name: ATS-4
missions.thruster: EOS 5 cm cesium contact ion engine
missions.target_or_role: Ion propulsion experiment (E-W stationkeeping thrusters, tested in low orbit)
missions.flight_performance: Combined ~10 h over 55 days, both engines throttled; first successful orbital ion-engine test; S/C potential -132 V
missions.notes: Centaur second burn failed: spacecraft stayed attached to the Centaur in a 218 x 760 km orbit instead of GEO.

missions.name: ATS-5
missions.thruster: EOS 5 cm cesium contact ion engine
missions.target_or_role: North-south stationkeeping demonstration
missions.flight_performance: Spacecraft could not be despun (76 rpm): cesium feed flooded, no beam extraction; used only as neutral plasma source for charging experiments
missions.notes: Reached space, never produced thrust.

missions.name: SERT-2
missions.thruster: NASA LeRC 15 cm mercury electron-bombardment (Kaufman) ion engine
missions.target_or_role: Long-duration ion thruster test
missions.flight_performance: Thrusters ran 3781 h and 2011 h (ended by grid shorts), up to 300 restarts, flight data 1970-1981; 28 mN at 4200 s
missions.notes: Launch often listed 3 Feb 1970 (US local) / 4 Feb UTC; NASA synopsis table gives 02.03.70.

missions.name: ATS-6
missions.thruster: EOS cesium electron-bombardment ion engine (8 cm class)
missions.target_or_role: North-south stationkeeping demonstration
missions.flight_performance: One engine ~1 h, the other 92 h; both failed to restart (cesium flooding of the discharge chamber)

missions.name: ETS-III (Kiku-4)
missions.thruster: MELCO 5 cm mercury electron-bombardment ion engine
missions.target_or_role: Engineering test satellite, ion engine experiment
missions.flight_performance: 2 mN, 2000 s per engine; ion engine operation demonstrated
missions.notes: ~1000 km, 45° orbit. NTRS 19850001794 (Kitamura 1984): two mercury electron-bombardment engines, 2 mN / 2000 s. JAXA page: orbit and end of operations 1985-03-08.

missions.name: ETS-VI (Kiku-6)
missions.thruster: MELCO 12 cm xenon Kaufman IES (20 mN class)
models: MELCO 20 mN-class xenon ion thruster, 1st generation (ETS-VI / COMETS IES)
missions.target_or_role: North-south stationkeeping demonstration
missions.flight_performance: Thrusters operated in orbit despite the apogee-engine failure that stranded the satellite in a highly elliptical orbit
missions.notes: Goebel/Katz give 13 cm grid; other sources 12 cm. Planned GEO not reached.

missions.name: COMETS (Kakehashi)
missions.thruster: MELCO xenon Kaufman IES (20 mN class, same system as ETS-VI)
models: MELCO 20 mN-class xenon ion thruster, 1st generation (ETS-VI / COMETS IES)
missions.target_or_role: Communications/broadcast engineering test satellite; ion engine stationkeeping demo
missions.flight_performance: Ion engine system launched (same EP subsystem as ETS-VI); in-orbit operation not documented in the cited source
missions.notes: H-II second-stage failure left it in the wrong orbit. Goebel ch.9 gives launch year 1996 (error; actual 21 Feb 1998). Number of thrusters not confirmed.

missions.name: Hayabusa (MUSES-C)
missions.target_or_role: Asteroid 25143 Itokawa sample return (primary propulsion)
missions.flight_performance: 39,637 thruster-unit-hours total, 47 kg Xe, ~2.2 km/s delta-V, ~25,590 h powered flight (final, before re-entry)
missions.notes: Microwave (ECR) discharge ion engines; return enabled by cross-connecting neutralizer of one unit with ion source of another after degradations.

missions.name: ETS-VIII (Kiku-8)
missions.thruster: MELCO 12 cm xenon Kaufman IES (20 mN class)
models: MELCO 20 mN-class xenon ion thruster (ETS-VIII IES)
missions.target_or_role: North-south stationkeeping
missions.flight_performance: >3000 thruster-hours over ~2.5 years of NSSK (eoPortal)

missions.name: Hodoyoshi-4
missions.thruster: MIPS (UTokyo/NESTRA miniature microwave ion propulsion system)
missions.target_or_role: Ion thruster demo on a ~50 kg-class (per UTokyo) microsatellite
missions.flight_performance: Ion acceleration for 6 min on 2014-10-28; UTokyo claims the first ion-thruster operation on a satellite of <100 kg (body text: <50 kg); MIPS 210 uN, 740 s
missions.notes: Launch 19 Jun 2014 UTC (20 Jun JST).

missions.name: Hayabusa2
missions.target_or_role: Ryugu sample return (capsule 2020-12-06); extended mission to 2001 CC21 (Torifune) flyby and 1998 KY26
missions.flight_performance: Round trip: ~1.3 km/s, 9,514 h powered flight (IAC-2021); by June 2026 total dV >2 km/s (155 % of requirement), engine B alone 8,143 h; A, C, D neutralizer degradation
missions.notes: Microwave (ECR) ion engines, improved mu10.

missions.name: PROCYON
missions.thruster: I-COUPS (UTokyo microwave ion thruster + cold gas)
missions.target_or_role: 50 kg deep-space microprobe; planned asteroid 2000 DP107 flyby
missions.flight_performance: 223 h cumulative, ~346 µN averaged thrust (5.62 mA beam). A grid short (suspected metal debris between the grids) from ~10 March 2015 ended operation; the 2000 DP107 flyby was cancelled.
missions.notes: Piggyback on Hayabusa2 launch.

missions.name: SLATS (Tsubame)
missions.thruster: MELCO/JAXA 20 mN class xenon ion engine (IES)
models: MELCO 20 mN-class xenon ion thruster (ETS-VIII IES)
missions.target_or_role: Super-low-altitude drag compensation
missions.flight_performance: Held 7 altitudes 271.5 to 167.4 km with the ion engine (plus RCS at 167.4 km); Guinness record lowest Earth-observation satellite

missions.name: Pale Blue PBI water ion thruster IOD (D-Orbit ION carrier, Transporter-14)
members: Pale Blue PBI water ion thruster IOD (D-Orbit ION carrier, Transporter-14)
missions.thruster: Pale Blue PBI (1U water ECR ion thruster)
models: Pale Blue PBI water ion thruster
missions.target_or_role: In-orbit demonstration of a water-propellant ion thruster
missions.flight_performance: 23/23 ignitions, 5.24 h cumulative steady-state thrust, ~0.35 mN
missions.notes: Host vehicle name and exact date not stated in the paper abstract (Transporter-14 flew 23 Jun 2025); gridded geometry assumed from 'ion beam current' telemetry - verify.

missions.name: EURECA
missions.target_or_role: RITA radio-frequency ion thruster experiment on the retrievable carrier
missions.flight_performance: ~240 h operation (secondary list; primary figure not found)
missions.notes: Launched on STS-46; first RIT flight; 240 h of operation per eoPortal

missions.name: ARTEMIS
missions.thruster: RIT-10 (RITA, Astrium DE) and UK-10/T5 (EITA, Astrium UK)
missions.target_or_role: Data-relay satellite; ion engines for NSSK, used to rescue the spacecraft from a 31,000 km orbit
missions.flight_performance: Ion engines raised the orbit over ~18 months; GEO reached 2003-01-31 by continuous firing of a single thruster after 3 of 4 thrusters went out of service
missions.notes: 2 RITA (RIT-10, DE) + 2 EITA (UK-10/T5 heritage, GB). Which thruster type carried the salvage is not stated in the cited sources.

missions.name: GOCE
missions.target_or_role: Gravity-field mission; continuous drag-free control at ~255-224 km
missions.flight_performance: Throttled 1-20 mN drag compensation for >4 years
missions.notes: QinetiQ T5 (one active, one redundant).

missions.name: BepiColombo (MTM)
missions.target_or_role: Mercury transfer (Solar Electric Propulsion System on the Mercury Transfer Module)
missions.status: SEP mission complete (final thrust arc ended 2026-06-15; MTM separated 2026-09-03; Mercury orbit insertion 2026-11-21)
missions.flight_performance: Up to 2 T6 at a time (max 290 mN). A 2024 power-system anomaly (unexpected currents between the solar array and the power unit) reduced the power available to the thrusters and forced a lower-thrust trajectory, delaying Mercury orbit insertion to Nov 2026.
missions.notes: QinetiQ T6 (Kaufman).

missions.name: Deep Space 1
missions.target_or_role: Technology validation; flybys of 9969 Braille and comet Borrelly
missions.flight_performance: 16,265 h of operation (JPL; NASA Glenn gives 16,246 h), >70 kg Xe
missions.notes: First ion primary propulsion in deep space.

missions.name: Dawn
missions.target_or_role: Orbiter of Vesta and Ceres
missions.flight_performance: 425 kg Xe loaded; 11.5 km/s total ion dV; ~5.9 years of thrusting
missions.notes: First spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies.

missions.name: DART
missions.target_or_role: Ion thruster technology demo on the Didymos/Dimorphos impact mission
missions.flight_performance: First activation 2021-12-18: 21 recycles in ~2 h of operation; a power-system-electronics anomaly coinciding with a recycle (misconfigured FPGA I/O pin; arc-induced EMI suspected) led to the suspension of further NEXT-C operations
missions.notes: Aerojet Rocketdyne NEXT-C; not used for primary propulsion.

missions.name: LunaH-Map
missions.target_or_role: Lunar polar hydrogen mapping 6U CubeSat (Artemis I)
missions.flight_performance: Iodine valve partially stuck; thruster never produced the required thrust; lunar orbit not reached
missions.notes: Busek iodine RF gridded ion thruster.

missions.name: Lunar IceCube
missions.target_or_role: Lunar water-ice 6U CubeSat (Artemis I)
missions.flight_performance: No confirmed thruster firing
missions.notes: Reached space; BIT-3 never confirmed fired.

missions.name: Hughes/Boeing HS-601HP satellites with XIPS-13
members: Orion 3 (1999-05-05; stranded by the Delta III upper-stage failure, XIPS use not confirmed)
missions.agency_or_operator: Hughes/Boeing for PanAmSat, SES, Satmex, DirecTV, AsiaSat, MEASAT, Orion
missions.target_or_role: Commercial comsats, XIPS north-south stationkeeping
missions.flight_performance: Tighe 2007: 60 flight 13 cm thrusters on 15 satellites, >120,500 h in orbit. Known XIPS failures: Galaxy 4R and Galaxy 10R (both primary and secondary XIPS lost by Aug 2004), PAS-6B (primary and then secondary lost by 2003), Satmex 5 (2010).
missions.notes: Member list from the Wikipedia EP list (17 incl. Orion 3, which was stranded by the Delta III upper-stage failure - XIPS use not confirmed) vs 15 satellites in Tighe 2007: membership not fully reconciled. Wikipedia also had ProtoStar-2/SES-7 (2009) and Superbird commented out (unverified, excluded). 4 thrusters each per Goebel (2 redundant pairs).

missions.name: Hughes/Boeing 702 and 702HP satellites with XIPS-25
missions.agency_or_operator: Hughes/Boeing (operators: Intelsat/PanAmSat, Telesat, Thuraya, XM/Sirius, DirecTV, USSF WGS, Inmarsat, SES, ViaSat)
missions.target_or_role: Comsats: XIPS orbit raising (optional) + all stationkeeping
missions.flight_performance: Goebel (~2008): 14 satellites / 56 thrusters launched; L3 (undated): >116 25 cm thrusters in orbit, >280,000 failure-free hours
missions.notes: Boeing: 702HP = bi-prop + xenon ion. Membership assembled from Gunter's 702 list; individual XIPS fit not verified for each satellite (Goebel's ~2008 count of 14 vs 16 listed through 2007). Excluded: NSS-8 (destroyed on Sea Launch pad 2007), 702MP (Intelsat EpicNG, ViaSat-3, JCSAT-18/Kacific-1: Boeing lists 702MP as dual-mode/arcjet; Wikipedia claims XIPS on JCSAT-18 - unverified), 702X/O3b mPOWER (propulsion not verified). Original 702 solar-concentrator power loss (Galaxy 11, PAS-1R, Anik F1, Thuraya-1, XM-1/2) is unrelated to XIPS.

missions.name: Boeing 702SP all-electric satellites
missions.target_or_role: All-electric orbit raising and stationkeeping
missions.flight_performance: First commercial all-electric GEO satellites (ABS-3A / Eutelsat 115W B, dual launch on Falcon 9)
missions.notes: Operators in BM/MX/LU/US; country set to US (manufacturer). SES-20/21 XIPS fit inferred from the 702SP all-electric design.

missions.name: Shijian-9A (SJ-9A)
missions.target_or_role: Technology demo; first Chinese ion thruster flight (with a Hall thruster)
missions.flight_performance: 'Hundreds of hours' in orbit (LIP)

missions.name: Shijian-13 (ChinaSat-16)
missions.target_or_role: High-throughput comsat; ion NSSK and orbit-raising test
missions.flight_performance: First Chinese comsat with electric propulsion
missions.notes: DFH-3B bus.

missions.name: Shijian-20 (SJ-20)
missions.target_or_role: DFH-5 platform technology verification
missions.flight_performance: In-orbit verification from May 2020, 60 h by June 2020, performance met criteria
missions.notes: note: the scielo paper says SJ-20 'entered orbit ... in October 2019'; the actual launch was 2019-12-27

missions.name: Beihangkongshi-1
missions.target_or_role: 12U CubeSat; first in-orbit iodine electric propulsion
missions.flight_performance: 11 firings to 2021-02-28, cumulative altitude change >3 km (Nature 599, 411, 2021)
missions.notes: ThrustMe (France) RF gridded iodine ion thruster.

missions.name: Tianwen-2
missions.thruster: LIP ion thruster (LIPS-300 per Wikipedia; model unconfirmed)
missions.target_or_role: Asteroid Kamo'oalewa sample return, then comet 311P
missions.flight_performance: Solar electric propulsion used in cruise and approach (2026)
missions.notes: Ion (not Hall) propulsion per Planetary Society; Wikipedia EP list gives LIPS-300 and wrong launch year 2026. Thruster model and count unverified.

missions.name: Meteor 1-10 (Meteor-1 No. 10, factory 18L), 'Eol-1' SPT flight test
missions.agency_or_operator: VNIIEM (spacecraft), OKB Fakel (propulsion 'Eol'), Kurchatov Institute IAE (thruster physics)
missions.target_or_role: Meteorological satellite; first in-space test of a Hall (stationary plasma) thruster, xenon
missions.flight_performance: First SPT test in space (operated 1972): ~200 h of thruster operation; with ~20 mN thrust the ~1.3 t satellite's orbit altitude was raised by ~17 km in ~170 h of operation.
missions.notes: Kim & Popov et al. (Electric Propulsion Activity in Russia, Table 1) list it as 'Meteor #18' (= factory number 18L), 1972, 2 SPT-60. Gunter gives Meteor-1 10 (18L), 1971-120A, launched 29.12.1971. Some sources call the 1971 thruster SPT-60 loosely; the propulsion system was named 'Eol' (Eol-1).

missions.name: Meteor-Priroda 1 (Meteor 1-18), 'Eol-2' SPT flight test
missions.target_or_role: Earth-resources satellite; second SPT flight test (propulsion system 'Eol-2', two thruster modules, two cathodes each)
missions.flight_performance: Thruster operation for more than 600 h; fine orbit control and orbit circularisation demonstrated; plume effect on solar arrays checked over >300 h.
missions.notes: Kim et al. Table 1: 1974, Meteor-Priroda #1, 2 SPT-60M. IEPC-2007-142 cites the 'Eol-2' on Meteor-Priroda results (1978 conference). Gunter's Meteor-1 page instead names Meteor-1 19 (1974-10-28) as an SPD-60 carrier: the identification of the 1974 satellite is therefore not fully certain. Identification flagged: Gunter names Meteor-1 19 (1974-10-28) as the 1974 SPD-60 carrier.

missions.name: Meteor-Priroda 2 series with SPT-50 orbit-correction systems
missions.target_or_role: Earth-resources satellites; first operational use of SPT for orbit correction / spacecraft positioning
missions.flight_performance: Thrust efficiency ~0.33 quoted for the flight SPT-50 (Kim et al. Table 1).
missions.notes: Kim et al. Table 1 lists 1976 Meteor-Priroda #2, 1977 Meteor-Priroda #2-2 and 1981 Meteor-Priroda #2-4, each with 2 SPT-50. Mapping to Meteor 1-25/1-28/1-31 from Gunter's Meteor-Priroda table. CONFLICTS: Wikipedia's list gives SPT-60 for the 1976 satellite; Gunter's Meteor-1 page says Meteor-1 25 carried SPD-60 and names Meteor-1 27 (1977-04-05, a standard Meteor-1) as the SPD-50 carrier, not 1-28. Russian Wikipedia also names 'Meteor 1-27' for SPT-50. Treat member identification as uncertain. [thruster: SPT-50 (Kim et al.); Meteor-Priroda 2-1 disputed: SPT-60 per Wikipedia EP list and Gunter]

missions.name: Astrofizika (Kosmos 1066)
missions.target_or_role: Astrophysics / experimental satellite on a Meteor-type bus; SPT orbit correction
missions.notes: Kim et al. Table 1: 1978, VNIIEM, 'Astrophysics', orbit correction, 2 SPT-50. Launch date from the Wikipedia EP list; Russian Wikipedia SPT article also names Kosmos-1066 for SPT-50.

missions.name: Potok (Geizer) data-relay satellites
missions.agency_or_operator: NPO PM (Krasnoyarsk, now ISS Reshetnev) for the Soviet/Russian military
missions.target_or_role: Military geostationary data relay (Geizer); first operational GEO use of SPT: final positioning and E-W station keeping
missions.flight_performance: Kosmos 1366 (1982) was the first spacecraft with SPT-70 (first flight of SPT-70). Thrust efficiency ~0.45 quoted for the flight SPT-70.
missions.notes: Spacecraft launched 1982-1991 are USSR (SU); Potok 8-10 (1994-2000) were launched by Russia. Kim et al. Table 1 counts 16 NPO PM Kosmos/Luch spacecraft x 4 SPT-70 (1982-2000) = these 10 Potok + 6 Luch/Luch-1 (see Luch entry; 10 + 5 launched = 15 listed by Gunter, the 16th may be counted differently). An NPO PM paper quoted in search results says 15 Potok and Luch spacecraft with 4 SPT-70 each were launched 1982-1999. [country: SU for Potok 1-7 (1982-1991); RU for Potok 8-10 (1994-2000)]

missions.name: Luch (Altair) and Luch-1 (Gelios) data-relay satellites
missions.agency_or_operator: NPO PM (Krasnoyarsk) / Soviet then Russian government
missions.target_or_role: Geostationary data relay (Mir and other spacecraft); SPT for positioning and station keeping
missions.notes: First three launched as USSR, last two by Russia. Gunter: four SPT-70 plus hydrazine attitude thrusters. Luch-1 (1995) thruster type/count from the Wikipedia EP list (4 SPT-70); Gunter's Luch page covers the Altair satellites. [country: SU (1985-1989 launches); RU for Luch 1994 and Luch-2 1 1995]

missions.name: Plazma-A (Kosmos 1818, Kosmos 1867), Topaz-1 reactor test satellites
missions.target_or_role: Flight test of the Topaz-1 thermionic space nuclear reactor; SPT powered by the reactor for orbit correction
missions.status: Retired (reactors shut down 1987-1988; in high LEO storage orbit)
missions.notes: Kim et al. Table 1: 1987, Arsenal, 'Plasma', orbit correction, '2x6 SPT-70' (2 spacecraft x 6 thrusters). Only nuclear-electric Hall-thruster flights to date.

missions.name: Gals communication satellites
missions.agency_or_operator: NPO PM (builder); Russian government / Kosmicheskaya Svyaz
missions.target_or_role: Direct-broadcast TV; SPT for positioning, E-W and N-S station keeping
missions.flight_performance: Gals-1 carried the first SPT-100 flown in space (1994).
missions.notes: Kim et al. Table 1: NPO PM, GALS (2 S/C), 2x8 SPT-100, positioning + E-W + N-S station keeping.

missions.name: Ekspress (first generation) and Ekspress-A (MSS-2500-GSO bus)
missions.agency_or_operator: NPO PM (builder); Russian Satellite Communications Company (RSCC)
missions.target_or_role: Communications; SPT for orbit correction / station keeping
missions.status: Retired (Ekspress-A1 lost at launch; A4 retired 2020 to graveyard)
missions.flight_performance: Ekspress-A4 reported an inclination-correction (N-S) thruster failure from 2004 (Russian Wikipedia).
missions.notes: Gunter: 8 x SPT-100 for both Ekspress and Ekspress-A. Russian Wikipedia describes the KAUR-4 platform as having 'four SPT-100 correction thrusters' (possibly counting active thrusters only). 5 of 6 reached orbit. Ekspress-A4 thruster prime noted as uncertain ('SPT-100(?) / KM-5') in Wikipedia's EP list.

missions.name: Kupon-1
missions.agency_or_operator: Central Bank of Russia (operator); NPO Lavochkin (prime, US-KMO bus)
missions.target_or_role: Communications (banking network)
missions.notes: Only source found is the Wikipedia EP list (4 SPT-70, OKB Fakel). Cause of the 1998 failure not identified in sources found; no evidence it was thruster related.

missions.name: Yamal-100 (Yamal 101, Yamal 102)
missions.agency_or_operator: RSC Energia (builder, USP bus); Gazkom / Gazprom Space Systems
missions.target_or_role: Communications
missions.status: Retired (Yamal 101 failed shortly after launch per Wikipedia; Yamal 102 retired)
missions.notes: RussianSpaceWeb: propulsion included eight SPD-70 (= SPT-70) xenon thrusters. Kim et al. Table 1 lists 'PSC Energiya, Yamal-100, SPT-70'. Fate of Yamal 101 not verified here.

missions.name: Yamal-200 (Yamal 201, Yamal 202)
missions.agency_or_operator: RSC Energia (builder, USP bus); Gazprom Space Systems
missions.target_or_role: Communications; SPT for station keeping
missions.status: Retired (Yamal 201 failed 2014-06-05; Yamal 202 replaced by Yamal 601 in 2019)
missions.notes: Gunter and Wikipedia: 8 x SPT-70 (OKB Fakel) for station keeping.

missions.name: Ekspress-AM (MSS-2500-GSO / MSS-767 bus, NPO PM)
missions.target_or_role: Communications; SPT for station keeping
missions.status: Mixed: AM11 retired 2006 after debris damage; AM1 decommissioned 2013; AM22 retired 2019; AM2 retired 2016; AM3, AM33, AM44 listed operational (Wikipedia)
missions.flight_performance: Ekspress-AM1: N-S station keeping no longer possible from April 2010 (Russian Wikipedia).
missions.notes: SPT-100 on the AM family confirmed by Wikipedia (SPT-100 used on the 'Ekspress A and AM constellations') and Russian Wikipedia (KAUR-4 platform: SPT-100 correction thrusters). Count 8 per spacecraft from the Wikipedia EP list for AM1/AM2/AM3 only; Russian Wikipedia says 'four SPT-100'. AM44 thruster variant SPT-100V from Russian Wikipedia. Not included: Ekspress-AM4/AM4R/AM7/AMU1 (Astrium/Airbus Eurostar-3000, Western-built).

missions.name: Ekspress-1000 / Ekspress-2000 generation Ekspress satellites (ISS Reshetnev)
missions.thruster: SPT-100 (SPT-100B/SPT-100V); Russian Wikipedia also names SPT-140 for the Ekspress-1000/2000 platforms
missions.target_or_role: Communications; SPT for orbit raising (final insertion into GEO) and station keeping
missions.status: Mostly operational; Ekspress-AT1 listed as failed in orbit (March 2026, Wikipedia); AM6 reached orbit only with own propulsion after a launch anomaly
missions.flight_performance: drop 'AM6 likewise' and 'reached orbit only with own propulsion after a launch anomaly' unless a source is added
missions.notes: SPT-100 for AM5, AM6, Ekspress-80/103 confirmed by the Reshetnev authors (journal) and Wikipedia; AT1 'four SPT-100 correction thrusters' only from a search snippet of Russian Wikipedia. SPT on AT2, AM8, AMU3, AMU7 inferred from the platform statement in Russian Wikipedia (Ekspress-1000/2000: SPT-100 and SPT-140 from Fakel) and AMU3/AMU7 electric orbit raising; per-satellite thruster counts not found. Excluded Western-built Russian-operated Ekspress: AM4, AM4R, AM7, AMU1 (Eurostar-3000). [thruster: SPT-100 family (Gunter: '? x SPT-100' for AM5 and AM6); model/count for AT1, AT2, AM8, Ekspress-80/103, AMU3, AMU7 per the Reshetnev journal paper where available]

missions.name: Yamal-401
missions.agency_or_operator: ISS Reshetnev (Ekspress-2000 bus); Gazprom Space Systems
missions.target_or_role: Communications
missions.notes: Thruster data only from the Wikipedia EP list. Yamal-402 (2012) and Yamal-601 (2019) are Thales Alenia Spacebus satellites (Western-built) and are NOT included here although Wikipedia lists SPT-100 on them.

missions.name: Kanopus-V Earth-observation satellites
missions.target_or_role: Disaster monitoring / Earth observation in sun-synchronous orbit; SPT-50 orbit correction
missions.status: Operational/partly retired (status not verified per satellite)
missions.notes: Gunter: 2 x SPT-50. MAI paper: Kanopus-V (450 kg) correction propulsion based on SPT-50 (search-result summary: two SPT-50, 26 kg fuelled, 14 mN nominal). Kanopus-V-IK launch date from RussianSpaceWeb (Gunter's table garbled). Kanopus-V 7/8 planned (2026), not counted. Belarusian BKA (same VNIIEM bus, 2012) not included: thrusters not confirmed.

missions.name: KazSat-1 and KazSat-2 (Khrunichev, Yakhta bus)
missions.target_or_role: Communications (Russian-built for Kazakhstan)
missions.status: KazSat-1 lost June 2008; KazSat-2 status not verified
missions.notes: Russian-built export spacecraft (include or drop according to page scope). Gunter: KazSat-1 eight SPT-70 + K10K engine. KazSat-2 SPT-70 from Russian Wikipedia and the Wikipedia EP list (8). The Wikipedia EP list gives KazSat-1 launch as 2005-06-18, which is wrong (Gunter: 2006-06-17).

missions.name: KazSat-3
missions.target_or_role: Communications (Russian-built for Kazakhstan)
missions.notes: Russian-built export spacecraft. Thruster count not listed.

missions.name: AMOS-5
missions.target_or_role: Communications (Russian-built export)
missions.notes: Russian-built export; include only if the page covers Russian-built spacecraft for foreign operators. Other Ekspress-1000 exports (Telkom-3 2012, stranded; AngoSat-2 2022) probably carry SPTs but were not confirmed and are not listed.

missions.name: SESAT 1 (later Eutelsat 16C)
missions.agency_or_operator: NPO PM (builder, Ekspress-A type bus); Eutelsat (operator)

missions.name: NASA Psyche

missions.flight_performance: All engineering systems nominal in 100-day checkout; thrusting nearly continuously in cruise (JPL, May 2024). Only one PPU and three thrusters needed to complete the mission. In April 2025 thrusting paused after a pressure drop in the primary xenon line (faulty valve); full thruster operation resumed on 2025-06-16 on the backup line. Mars gravity assist completed (May 2026); thrusting toward the asteroid again (NASA, 22 Oct 2026); arrival Aug 2029.
missions.notes: First Hall thrusters beyond lunar distance. Thrusters built by Fakel (RU) for Maxar; 'SPT-140D' naming as Maxar/Fakel variant.
